newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian brokers rate Bekaert a "hold".
newsitem.headline: Belgian brokers rate Bekaert a "hold".

text.p: Belgium's Generale Bank and brokerage Vermeulen Raemdonck/BBL said on Wednesday they maintained their "hold" recommendation for shares in steel cord and wire maker Bekaert NV, despite an acquisition announcement.
Bekaert said on Tuesday it had acquired British Steel's 40-percent stake in TWIL, lifting its participation in the British steel wire maker to 100 percent.
"It remains a 'hold' share," Generale Bank said.
"The acquisition did not have an effect on our recommendation -- the effects will come in the long term," Generale Bank analyst Sandra Vandersmissen said.
"It's within the strategy of Bekaert to consolidate their leadership in wire manufacturing," she added.
Brokerage Vermeulen said it also retained its hold recommendation on Bekaert and kept its earnings per share estimate unchanged at 1,100 francs for 1997.

"Holding 100 percent of TWIL should enable Bekaert to reap the full benefits once the restructuring, which will be accelerated as part of the new structural profit improvement programme announced in December 1996, is completed by the second-half of 1998," Generale Bank said in a research note.
By 1300 GMT Bekaert shares were up 0.46 percent at 21,800 francs, but well below their all-time high of 32,675 francs reached on March 7 last year.
-- Paul de Bendern, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6815, Fax +32 2 230 7710
